# Tax rates – Australian resident

These income tax rates apply to individuals who are Australian residents for tax purposes for the full income year.

The rates below **do not include the Medicare levy of 2%**.

Use these rates to work out the tax on your taxable income for the relevant income year.

# Study and training loan repayment thresholds and rates

These repayment thresholds and rates apply to all study and training support loans, including:

- Higher Education Loan Program (HELP)
- VET Student Loan (VSL)
- Student Financial Supplement Scheme (SFSS)
- Student Start-up Loan (SSL)
- ABSTUDY Student Start-up Loan
- Australian Apprenticeship Support Loan (AASL)

You begin making compulsory repayments when your repayment income is above the minimum repayment threshold for that income year. Compulsory repayments are made through your tax return.

# Study and training loan repayment thresholds and rates

These repayment thresholds and rates apply to all study and training support loans, including:

- Higher Education Loan Program (HELP)
- VET Student Loan (VSL)
- Student Financial Supplement Scheme (SFSS)
- Student Start-up Loan (SSL)
- ABSTUDY Student Start-up Loan
- Australian Apprenticeship Support Loan (AASL)

You begin making compulsory repayments when your repayment income is above the minimum repayment threshold for that income year. Compulsory repayments are made through your tax return.

text:
## Repayment thresholds and rates 2025–26

From the 2025–26 income year, compulsory repayments are calculated using **marginal rates**. This means the repayment is calculated only on the income above the minimum threshold, rather than on your total repayment income.

The minimum repayment income threshold for 2025–26 is **$67,000**.

| Repayment income | Repayment |
| --- | --- |
| $0 – $67,000 | Nil |
| $67,001 – $125,000 | 15c for each $1 over $67,000 |
| $125,001 – $179,285 | $8,700 plus 17c for each $1 over $125,000 |
| $179,286 and over | 10% of total repayment income |

## Repayment thresholds and rates 2024–25

For 2024–25, a single percentage rate applied to your **total** repayment income once you reached a bracket.

The minimum repayment income threshold for 2024–25 was **$54,435**.

| Repayment income | Rate applied to total repayment income |
| --- | --- |
| Below $54,435 | Nil |
| $54,435 – $62,850 | 1.0% |
| $62,851 – $66,620 | 2.0% |
| $66,621 – $70,618 | 2.5% |
| $70,619 – $74,855 | 3.0% |
| $74,856 – $79,346 | 3.5% |
| $79,347 – $84,107 | 4.0% |
| $84,108 – $89,154 | 4.5% |
| $89,155 – $94,503 | 5.0% |
| $94,504 – $100,174 | 5.5% |
| $100,175 – $106,185 | 6.0% |
| $106,186 – $112,556 | 6.5% |
| $112,557 – $119,309 | 7.0% |
| $119,310 – $126,467 | 7.5% |
| $126,468 – $134,056 | 8.0% |
| $134,057 – $142,100 | 8.5% |
| $142,101 – $150,626 | 9.0% |
| $150,627 – $159,663 | 9.5% |
| $159,664 and over | 10.0% |

Repayment income is your taxable income plus any total net investment loss, total reportable fringe benefits amounts, reportable super contributions and exempt foreign employment income.
